chunks: Ibn Mahbub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Burayd al-'Ijli, who said:

Abu Ja'far عليه السلام was asked about a man against whom witnesses testified that he had broken the fast of Ramadan for three days. He said: “He is to be asked: ‘Is there upon you any sin in your breaking the fast?’ If he says, ‘No,’ then it is upon the Imam to kill him; and if he says, ‘Yes,’ then it is upon the Imam to punish him severely with beating.”

key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the Imam as the lawful authority
key_terms.يَنْهَكَهُ ضَرْبًا: to punish him severely with beating

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on someone who repeatedly breaks the fast in Ramadan and denies its sinfulness?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a man proven by witnesses to have deliberately broken the fast in Ramadan for three days. The ruling distinguishes between one who denies the sinfulness of the act, indicating a more severe doctrinal implication, and one who acknowledges it as sinful, for whom corporal punishment is prescribed.
